metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 30. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.text: Chapter 1
yac candraprabhavaṃ varāmbaragataṃ yal liṅgasaṃjñaṃ jalaṃ sa prāṇas tadadhaḥ sthiraṃ ca kamalaṃ dhatte mukhordhvaṃ hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: That water born from the moon, situated in the excellent sky and called the <s>liṅga</s>, is the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath); below it, firm in the heart, it supports a lotus with its mouth turned upward.

children.text: baddhvā kumbhakam ātmagāḍharacitaṃ tad brahmanāḍīgataṃ hy ānetuṃ vadane ṣaḍadhvagakalā saivaṃvidhā sāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath retention), formed firmly within oneself, in order to bring that which has entered the <s>brahmanāḍī</s> to the mouth, this is the kind of <s>sāraṇā</s> connected with the six-path kalā.

children.text: Chapter 2
ghaṇṭākoṭikapolakoṭarakuṭījihvāgramadhyāśrayācchaṅkhinyāgatarājadantavivaraṃ prāntordhvavaktreṇa yat ||
children.translated_text: From its seat at the tip of the tongue, in the hollow chamber between the bell-like uvula and the cheek, what has come through the <s>śaṅkhinī</s> to the opening of the royal teeth, with the mouth-end turned upward,

children.text: samprāptaṃ hanurandhramūlavidhinā yac candratoyaṃ mukhe tat sarvaṃ ravikālarūpasadane rakṣet parā sāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: that lunar water which has reached the mouth by the method at the root of the jaw-opening: all of it should be protected in the abode whose form is the sun and time. This is the supreme <s>sāraṇā</s>.

children.text: Chapter 3
nṛtyan nityordhvajihvo yadi pibati pumān vaktradhārāmṛtaughaṃ susvādaṃ śītalāṅgaṃ duritabhayaharaṃ kṣutpipāsāvināśi ||
children.translated_text: If a man, with his tongue always moving upward, drinks the stream from the mouth, a flood of nectar that is sweet-tasting, cool in the body, remover of the fear of sin, and destroyer of hunger and thirst,

children.text: piṇḍasthairyaṃ yad asmād bhavati bata mahāmṛtyurogā dravante daurbhāgyaṃ yāti nāśaṃ harati viṣajarāṃ yāti kāle bhramitvā ||
children.translated_text: then from this there comes firmness of the body; great death and diseases, alas, run away; misfortune goes to destruction, and after moving about in time it removes poison and old age.

children.text: Chapter 4
jihvāgraṃ tv atha rājadantavivaraṃ nītvā tato ghaṇṭikāṃ saṃsthāpya pratijihvaparva śaśino mārge kalāṃ ca kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having brought the tip of the tongue to the opening of the royal teeth and from there to the uvula, one should set each joint of the tongue in place and cast the <s>kalā</s> onto the path of the moon.

children.text: evaṃsāraṇike patanti ca sudhādhārāḥ punaḥ ṣaṇmukhagāndhārāpy atha tatkalāpamathanaṃ nāḍīmukhojjṛmbhaṇam ||
children.translated_text: When this <s>sāraṇā</s> is performed, streams of nectar fall; then there is also the Gandhāra of the six mouths, the churning of that <s>kalā</s>, and the opening of the mouths of the channels.

children.text: Chapter 5
prāṇavātena nītvordhvaṃ koṭare candrajāṃ kalām ||
children.translated_text: Having carried upward by the breath the moon-born <s>kalā</s> in the cavity,

children.text: manthitāṃ divyajātāṃ ca tena gāndhārakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: churned and divinely produced by that Gandhāra action,

children.text: Chapter 6
nāsāpaścimamārgavāhapavanāt prāṇe 'tidīrghīkṛte candrāmbu pratisāraṇāṃ sukṛtinaḥ prāgghaṇṭikāyāḥ pathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the <s>prāṇa</s> has been greatly lengthened by the wind moving along the rear path of the nose, the meritorious man sprinkles the lunar water along the path before the uvula by <s>pratisāraṇā</s>.

children.text: siñcan kālaviśālavahnivaśagaṃ bhūtvā sa nāḍīśataṃ tat kāryaṃ kurute punar navatanuṃ jīrṇadrumaskandhavat ||
children.translated_text: Having come under the power of the vast fire of time, he then makes the hundred channels perform that action, producing a renewed body like the trunk of an old tree.

children.text: Chapter 7
protkṣiptaṃ vṛṣaṇasya golakayugaṃ madhye dhvajaṃ proddhvajaṃ nityordhve bata śaṅkhasāraṇavidhau vaktraṃ vidheyaṃ nijam ||
children.translated_text: The pair of testicular globes is thrown upward, the penis in the middle is raised up; in the method of <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s>, indeed, one's own mouth is always to be directed upward.

children.text: sarvasthānaśarīrabandhanavaśāt skandhoddhṛtānāṃ yathā nāḍīnāṃ mukhataḥ sudhānidhijalaṃ siñcann adho gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Because of the binding of the body in all places, as it sprinkles the water of the nectar-ocean from the mouths of the channels drawn up from the shoulders, it goes downward.

children.text: Chapter 8
vṛṣaṇākarṣaṇaṃ kāryam athavā śaṅkhasāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: One should perform the drawing up of the testicles, or else <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s>.

children.text: bodhanaṃ caiva kuṇḍalyās tiṣṭhec caivotkaṭāsanam ||
children.translated_text: There is also the awakening of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, and one should remain in <s>utkaṭāsana</s>.

children.text: Chapter 9
paścād āsanaśuddhavātanikarān ādāya kaṇṭhavraṇāt saṃsthāpyā ravimaṇḍale tu bhujagī sambhūtanāḍītrayāt ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, having taken in the masses of purified breath from the posture and placed the serpent-power at the throat aperture, in the solar orb, from the three channels that have arisen,

children.text: devī madhyapathoditā prakurute kampaṃ tato mūrchanāṃ dūrakarṣaṇadarśanaṃ śrutigaṇāṃś cānyā mahāsāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: the goddess, rising in the middle path, produces trembling and then swooning, distant attraction, vision, hosts of sounds, and other effects. This is the great <s>sāraṇā</s>.

children.text: Chapter 10
ādhārāmbujakośakandabhujagī sambhūya nāḍītrayāt candrārkodbhavanāḍikordhvayugalaṃ cādvaitapathyāgatam ||
children.translated_text: The serpent-power, arising from the bulb in the sheath of the base-lotus and from the three channels, has come to the upper pair of channels born of moon and sun, along the nondual path.

children.text: tatraivāṅgulibhir nipīḍya kramaśaḥ śāntiṃ mano mārutaṃ candro yāti raviṃ tataś ca bhuvane tulyā mahāsāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: There, pressing successively with the fingers, one should calm the mind and breath; the moon goes to the sun, and then in the world this is the comparable great <s>sāraṇā</s>.

children.text: sūryāntaḥ śaśivīcidantavadanaprāntaplavaughoragī samprāpte pavanātisaṅgaharaṇe kṣipraṃ tato dhāvitā ||
children.translated_text: When the serpent-power, like a flood at the mouth-edge within the teeth of the moon-wave inside the sun, has arrived at the removal of the excessive contact of breath, it then rushes quickly onward.

children.text: śrīmanmadhyapathāntato vidadhatī kampādi kopānvitā tasyaivāśrayayāyino 'pi śaśino dattā sudhā saṃmatā ||
children.translated_text: Coming to the end of the splendid middle path, causing trembling and the like and filled with fury, it grants the approved nectar of that very moon even to one who has resorted to it.

children.text: ādau śoṣaṇiko 'tra sāraṇam ataḥ kāryaṃ mahāsāraṇaṃ kartavyaṃ pratisāraṇaṃ ca guruṇā nirdiṣṭamārgaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Here the drying procedure comes first; therefore <s>sāraṇa</s> should be performed, then <s>mahāsāraṇa</s>, and <s>pratisāraṇa</s> should be done in sequence by the path taught by the guru.

children.text: paścād eva ca śaṅkhasāraṇavidhau kāryaṃ mahāsāraṇaṃ sammūrchā vitatākṛtiḥ pratidinaṃ velātrayaṃ dīyatām ||
children.translated_text: Only afterward, in the method of <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s>, should <s>mahāsāraṇa</s> be performed; a full-formed swoon should be induced every day at the three times.

children.text: ākuñcyāgajakāmarūpam acalaṃ bandhatvajātaṃ tanau nātyūrdhve caturaṅgulāgravidite sthāne hṛdā prāṇite ||
children.translated_text: Having contracted the unmoving form of elephant-desire, the state of bondage born in the body, at the place known to be four finger-breadths above, but not too high, and brought the breath there by the heart,

children.text: dantair bandhurite ca vātayugale praśleṣaṇāśleṣaṇāt nābhigranthivimokṣapātasahaje mārge manaḥsiddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the two winds are held by the teeth, through joining and separating, on the natural path of the release and fall of the navel-knot, there arise attainments of the mind.

children.text: dūrākāravisarpite ca pavane nābheś ca mārgasthite bandheṣu triṣu satsu so 'pi śithile madhyaprabodhe sati ||
children.translated_text: When the breath has spread into a distant form and is situated on the path of the navel, when the three locks are present and even that is loosened, and when the middle is awakened,

children.text: kṣipraṃ ca dhriyate dvipīṭhamaruto 'py ūrdhvakramākarṣaṇe saṃyukto gaticittaśoṣaṇam ataḥ prāpye 'nile tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: it is quickly held in the upward-sequential drawing of the two-seat winds; joined with motion, it remains when the drying up of thought is reached in the breath.

children.text: mūle mūlordhvacakre vṛṣaṇakulatale vahnimātaṅgakūle kampakṣobhabhramāḍhye dhvanitaparicayaṃ gharmapātordhvaroma ||
children.translated_text: At the root, in the root's upper wheel, at the base of the group of testicles, on the bank of the fire-elephant, there is trembling, agitation, and dizziness, acquaintance with sound, falling sweat, and hair standing on end.

children.text: bhūmityāgaṃ kavitvaṃ parapuraviśanaṃ vaśyam ākarṣaṇaṃ ca hy evaṃ vā cetanāptā prabhavati nikhilā khecaratvapratiṣṭhā ||
children.translated_text: Abandoning the ground, poetic power, entering another's body, subjugation, and attraction also arise; thus, when consciousness has been attained, the whole establishment of the state of moving in the sky becomes effective.

children.text: dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: Two <s>brahmans</s> are to be known: <s>śabdabrahman</s> (brahman as sound) and that which is supreme.

children.text: hṛdaye parame dhāmni madhye tu ravicandramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the heart, in the supreme abode, in the middle are the sun and the moon.

children.text: nādaṃ tu taṃ gṛhītvā ca caitanyaṃ tatra yojayet
children.translated_text: Having grasped that <s>nāda</s> (resonance), one should join consciousness there.

children.text: dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>brahmans</s> are to be known: <s>śabdabrahman</s> and that which is supreme.

children.text: śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati
children.translated_text: One who is immersed in <s>śabdabrahman</s> attains the supreme <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: anyat sarvaṃ parityajya śabdabrahma sadābhyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned everything else, one should always practice <s>śabdabrahman</s>.

children.text: svasaṃvedyam asaṃvedyaṃ śabdabrahma dvidhā sthitam
children.translated_text: <s>Śabdabrahman</s> is established in two forms: self-experienced and not experienced.

children.text: cinoti prathamaḥ śabdaś ciñcinoti dvitīyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first sound is ci; the second is ciñci.

children.text: vivaraś ca tṛtīyaḥ syāc chaṅkhaśabdaś caturthakaḥ
children.translated_text: The third is vivara, and the fourth is the sound of the conch.

children.text: pañcamo meghanirghoṣaḥ ṣaṣṭham etad udīraṇam ||
children.translated_text: The fifth is the rumbling of a cloud; the sixth is this utterance.

children.text: saptamaṃ kāṃsyatālākhyaṃ meghaśabdas tathāṣṭamam
children.translated_text: The seventh is called the sound of bronze cymbals, and the eighth is likewise the sound of a cloud.

children.text: navamo 'py agnidāhaś ca daśamo dundubhisvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ninth is also the burning of fire, and the tenth is the sound of a kettledrum.

children.text: anāhataninādo 'yaṃ pavanāntavinirgataḥ
children.translated_text: This unstruck resonance issues forth at the end of the breath.

children.text: dhvanitena vinā yas tu nādaś caivam apaṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But that <s>nāda</s> (resonance) which is without a sounding cause is thus “unlearned.”

children.text: cinoti rasam uddhṛtya ciñcinoti bhagāśritam
children.translated_text: It gathers the <s>rasa</s> (vital fluid) after drawing it upward; resting in the <s>bhaga</s> (generative center), it makes the ciñ-ci sound.

children.text: virasāṃśena samprāptaṃ meghaśabdena cāviśet ||
children.translated_text: One should enter, by means of the cloud-sound, what has been reached through the portion devoid of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: majjāṃ patati nirghoṣaḥ saṃsthitodadhibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The roar, terrifying as the settled ocean, falls into the marrow.

children.text: kāṃsyatāle nabhaḥśabdaḥ prāṇameghadhvaniḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: At the bronze-cymbal stage there is the sound of the sky, and then the cloudlike resonance of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath).

children.text: jīvaś caivāgnidāhaḥ syān mokṣaḥ samaraso bhavet
children.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> (individual life) itself is the burning of fire, while <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) becomes a state of complete sameness.

children.text: viśuddham ittham ātmānaṃ paśyeta cātmanātmani ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should behold the purified self, by the self, within the self.

children.text: prathame janavātsalyaṃ dvitīye roganāśanam
children.translated_text: At the first stage there is affection from people; at the second, the destruction of disease.

children.text: tṛtīyena kavitvaṃ ca dūrākarṣaṃ caturthake ||
children.translated_text: Through the third comes poetic ability, and at the fourth, attraction from afar.

children.text: pañcame vāci kāmitvaṃ ṣaṣṭhe bhūmiṃ parityajet
children.translated_text: At the fifth there is mastery of speech; at the sixth, one leaves the ground.

children.text: saptame dūram ālokya cāṣṭame vajravad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: At the seventh one sees far away, and at the eighth one becomes like a thunderbolt.

children.text: navame sphurate kāyo daśame sāmarasyakam
children.translated_text: At the ninth the body throbs; at the tenth there is the state of complete sameness.

children.text: pṛthvīmadhye bhavet pṛthvī cāpām āpas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Earth becomes absorbed within earth, and waters likewise within waters.

children.text: tejomadhye bhavet tejo vāyur vāyau pralīyate
children.translated_text: Fire becomes absorbed within fire, and wind dissolves into wind.

children.text: ākāśo līyate sarvaḥ satattvaḥ piṇḍasaṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ether dissolves entirely, together with the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) and the aggregate of the body.

children.text: anāhato divārātrau dhvanate tu dhanaṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> sounds the unstruck resonance day and night.

children.text: tatrārūḍho yadā yogī prāpnuyāt paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: When the yogin has ascended there, he attains the supreme state.
